overdose_risk: Exceeding 4000 mg/day saturates glucuronidation/sulfation causing toxic NAPQI accumulation and fatal centrilobular hepatic necrosis.
Exceeding 2400 mg/day significantly elevates risk of acute interstitial nephritis, papillary necrosis, and massive upper GI hemorrhage.
Exceeding 2550 mg/day increases systemic accumulation and triggers profound lactic acidosis without incremental glycemic control.
High doses cause salicylate toxicity (salicylism), tinnitus, respiratory alkalosis followed by metabolic acidosis and cerebral edema.
Doses exceeding 80 mg/day dramatically increase myopathy and fatal rhabdomyolysis risks.
Excessive doses can provoke neurotoxicity, interstitial nephritis, and crystalluria.
Exceeding 1500 mg/day increases CNS excitation, seizure risk, and QT prolongation.
Exceeding 200 mg/day substantially increases risk of Serotonin Syndrome and ventricular arrhythmia (QTc prolongation).
Exceeding 400 mg/day drastically elevates risk of tonic-clonic seizures and fatal respiratory depression.
Doses above 80 mg/day do not confer extra blood pressure reduction and trigger severe hypotension and hyperkalemia.
High doses lead to severe bradycardia, cardiogenic shock, and atrioventricular block.
Excessive diuresis causes profound hypovolemia, circulatory collapse, and permanent ototoxicity.
High doses provoke severe hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, and cardiac arrest.
Exceeding 100 mg per single intake precipitates acute severe hypotension, priapism, and non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
Excessive sublingual nitrate leads to severe rebound hypotension, syncope, and reduced coronary perfusion.
High prolonged doses cause severe hypomagnesemia and impair calcium absorption.
High doses heighten hypomagnesemia, Clostridioides difficile colitis, and drug interaction risks.
